fields.markdown:
**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 274 **Price** 459 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- This top has 20 divisions, painted in a chaotic mess of clashing colors. When spun, the top quickly settles on a side and generates a strange magical effect based on the side that lands face-up. **Activate—Spin the Top** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Effect** Choose a creature within 60 feet to target and roll a d20 on the table below to determine the top's effect. You make any decisions for a spell cast by the top unless otherwise indicated, except that it must target the creature you chose, or the creature you chose must be the center of the spell's area, if it has an area but no targets. If the spell's range is less than 60 feet, increase the range to 60 feet.
Any spell DC required is DC 27, and any spell attack roll required is +17. If the top casts a spell on you, you don't get a saving throw or other defense against it. The top can't be activated again for 1d4 hours.
d20Madcap Top Effect
1You spin just like the top. You are [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) for 1 round and then [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) for 1 round.
2[_Slow_](/Spells.aspx?ID=289) affects the target.
3[_Shrink_](/Spells.aspx?ID=284) affects you for 1 day.
4A 3rd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159) makes you look like the target.
5A statue of the target, made of chocolate or candy, appears adjacent to you.
6Gravity reverses, sending you and the target 30 feet in the air, [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24). You both fall at the start of your next turn.
7[_Mind reading_](/Spells.aspx?ID=194) affects the target, and the top loudly recites what it discovers.
8[_Laughing fit_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1583) affects the target.
9A fountain erupts from the top, spraying wine for 10 minutes.
10[_Translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) affects you, but you teleport through Hell.
11[_Invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) affects you.
12Four singing skeletons appear to serenade you and your allies for 1 minute, granting a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks.
13The top flings 1 cp at you.
14[_Confusion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=48) affects the target.
15You and the target change places; this is a teleportation effect.
16[_Banishment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=19) affects the target, or paralyze if the target's on its home plane.
17Rainbow dye explodes and covers you for 24 hours.
18The top creates a [_toxic cloud_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1722) centered on the target.
19A random unattended object within 60 feet of you sprouts animal legs and follows you, reverting when the top's activation recharges.
20Spin again, and the target also spins as though it had activated the top.

---

A maelstromic destabilizer is a whirling gyroscope of burnished bronze and glass. It strengthens the bonds that hold a creature to this world by weakening those same bonds to every other nearby creature. When activated, the destabilizer emits a constant pleasant chime as it spins. For the next minute, the creature holding the gadget gains the listed resistance to spirit damage, while all creatures not immune to spirit damage in a 10-foot emanation gain the listed weakness to spirit damage.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 70

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents also have access to all assistive items from Morhen’s Mobility Apparel_

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 6
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _maestro's chair_ is a [traveler's chair](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1356) with the [impulse control](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1361) upgrade and a small pipe organ installed into the frame. You can use the maestro's chair to make [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks in the same manner that you could use any mundane instrument, using both of your hands. When you make a Performance check using your chair, you gain a +1 item bonus to the check.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per 10 minutes;   **Effect** You use your chair to Stride up to your chair's speed. If you have a [composition](/Traits.aspx?ID=31) cantrip that is currently active, you Sustain it as a free action.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This hat comes in many forms, such as a colorful turban or a pointy hat with a brim, and is adorned with symbols or runes. It grants you a +1 item bonus to Arcana checks and allows you to cast the [_prestidigitation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=229) cantrip as an arcane innate cantrip.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 650 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This larger, fancier hat grants a +2 bonus and can be activated. Each greater mage's hat has a specific 4th-rank summon spell from the arcane list woven into its fabric, typically [_summon animal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=316) or [_summon elemental_](/Spells.aspx?ID=320). If you prepare arcane spells, you can change the spell to a different 4th-rank arcane summon spell you know when you invest it. 

**Activate—Hat Spell** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You doff the hat, causing magical energy to pour from it. You cast the spell stored in the hat.

[Magekiller Bullet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5039)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Curse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=38" />
<trait label="Force" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=75" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 213

**Price** 1,500 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** round or sling bullet

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Magekiller bullets_ are forged by carving a spellcaster's bones with sigils of unbinding, grinding them to powder, and sealing the powder within the core of specially made rounds or sling bullets. When an activated _magekiller bullet_ hits a target, the ammunition burrows deep into its body and interferes with its connection to magic. Each time within the next week an affected target [Casts a Spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=3144), it must attempt a DC 11 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). On a failure, it takes 2d12 force damage. This curse can be counteracted with [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) as normal, but if the ammunition is first removed from the target with a successful DC 35 [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check and an operation that takes 1 hour, the counteract check gains a +4 circumstance bonus.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

A mageslayer deals an additional 1d6 spirit damage to any creature it Strikes that’s capable of casting spells from the arcane tradition. When wearing or wielding a mageslayer, you gain resistance 5 to damage from spells from the arcane tradition.

A suit of magic armor is simply a suit of armor or explorer’s clothing etched with fundamental runes. An armor potency rune increases the armor’s item bonus to AC, and a resilient rune adds an item bonus to saving throws.

 The Prices here are for all types of armor. You don’t need to adjust the Price from leather armor to full plate or the like. These armors are made of standard materials, not precious materials such as mithral.

fields.text: Item 5+ Magic Armor Invested Magical Source GM Core pg. 229 Usage worn armor Bulk varies by armor A suit of magic armor is simply a suit of armor or explorer’s clothing etched with fundamental runes. An armor potency rune increases the armor’s item bonus to AC, and a resilient rune adds an item bonus to saving throws. The Prices here are for all types of armor. You don’t need to adjust the Price from leather armor to full plate or the like. These armors are made of standard materials, not precious materials such as dawnsilver. Item 5 Magic Armor (+1) Source GM Core pg. 229, Core Rulebook pg. 556 Price 160 gp This armor has a +1 armor potency rune (increase the item bonus to AC by 1). Item 8 Magic Armor (+1 Resilient) Source GM Core pg. 229, Core Rulebook pg. 556 Price 500 gp This armor has a +1 armor potency rune (increase the item bonus to AC by 1) and a resilient rune (+1 item bonus to saves). Item 11 Magic Armor (+2 Resilient) Source GM Core pg. 229, Core Rulebook pg. 556 Price 1,400 gp This armor has a +2 armor potency rune (increase the item bonus to AC by 2) and a resilient rune (+1 item bonus to saves). Item 14 Magic Armor (+2 Greater Resilient) Source GM Core pg. 229, Core Rulebook pg. 556 Price 4,500 gp This armor has a +2 armor potency rune (increase the item bonus to AC by 2) and a greater resilient rune (+2 item bonus to saves). Item 18 Magic Armor (+3 Greater Resilient) Source GM Core pg. 229, Core Rulebook pg. 556 Price 24,000 gp This armor has a +3 armor potency rune (increase the item bonus to AC by 3) and a greater resilient rune (+2 item bonus to saves). Item 20 Magic Armor (+3 Major Resilient) Source GM Core pg. 229, Core Rulebook pg. 556 Price 70,000 gp This armor has a +3 armor potency rune (increase the item bonus to AC by 3) and a major resilient rune (+3 item bonus to saves).

fields.markdown:
**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 240 **Usage** held in 1 hand --- A _magic weapon_ is a weapon etched with only fundamental runes. A _weapon potency_ rune gives an item bonus to attack rolls with the weapon, and a _striking rune_ increases the weapon's number of weapon damage dice.

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 68

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents also have access to all assistive items from Morhen’s Mobility Apparel_

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These curved hearing aids hook over the top and sit behind your ear, with a receiver that fits into the ear opening. The external part of the device detects sound waves and, using divination magic, transfers them down the receiver and into your ear. You can wear one or two depending on your hearing loss, and you can turn your hearing aids on or off using an Interact action.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Military leaders or heads of state award these special medals to commend exemplary performance by their top soldiers. They’re typically worn on a special strip of fabric near the lapel, but soldiers from different countries sometimes wear them in other places. No matter how many _magical medals_ you have, they collectively count as one invested item.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Gorilla’s Might
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 25 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This steel medal resembles the head and upper body of a [gorilla](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2827). It’s typically given in recognition of physical prowess, and it grants you a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), and [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378).

**Activate—Gorila's Second Leap** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would fail but not critically fail an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378);  **Effect** The gorilla on the medal beats its chest, giving you another chance. You reroll the failed check.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Griffon’s Heart
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This copper medal features a [griffon’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3034) face, wings, and talons in profile. It is given in recognition of remarkable bravery, and it grants you a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects. While wearing this pendant, you can also cast [_forbidding ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1535) as an [innate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2901) cantrip.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of the Wolf Pack
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

There are three [wolf’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3241) heads engraved on this pewter medal, typically awarded to squads who demonstrate exceptional teamwork. While wearing the _medal of the wolf pack_, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against enemies you are [flanking](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 12"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Unicorn’s Purity
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 1,700 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The profile of the [unicorn](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=504) on this silver medal has a horn that extends slightly beyond the circular border. This medal is awarded in recognition of true righteousness and exemplary service to a cause.

**Activate—Unicorn’s Grace** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would regain Hit Points from a [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) effect;  **Effect** You regain an additional 4d6 Hit Points.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 16"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Phoenix’s Fire
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 9,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The [phoenix](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3137) on this gold medal is proud and fierce, and the medal features a border shaped like a flame. This medal is considered the highest honor in many countries and is awarded to those soldiers who have truly exemplified the ethics of their country through unbelievable service.

**Activate—Phoenix’s Sacrifice** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition increases;  **Effect** The phoenix bursts into flames. You lose the dying condition and regain 1 Hit Point. Your [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) value does not increase. You can use this action while [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95).

</title>

<column gap="tiny">

</row>

---

This prosthetic eye converts visible light into a telepathic signal that is relayed to the wearer's mind using divination magic. As the wearer's mind must process the telepathic signal in the same way as it would a nerve impulse, the acuity and other abilities related to the vision provided by the _magical prosthetic eye_ matches that of other members of your ancestry (for instance, a [goblin](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=4) with a magical prosthetic eye would be able to see in [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415), while a [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6) wearing the same prosthetic would need illumination). You can remove or replace a _magical prosthetic eye_ using an Interact action.

[Magnet Coin](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2562)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Highhelm](/Sources.aspx?ID=204) pg. 87

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Thera Heartslip commissioned these magical coins during her early thievery days and still has a number on hand to share with her confidants. This coin resembles an ordinary coin, but it's warm and seems to thrum slightly when touched. The coin's face features a very small fragment from the pressed portion that can be removed, such as a small star or one eye from the head on the face. Removing this fragment causes the coin to stop thrumming and feeling warm to the touch. Noticing the removed piece requires close inspection and a successful DC 19 Perception check.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You are holding the coin fragment; **Effect** You focus on the rest of the coin, imagining its complete form in your hand. The rest of the coin teleports into your hand, reforming the complete coin. If it was near any other coins, it also teleports up to 3d10 coins with it into your hand. The coin can only teleport up to 15 miles; if you are farther when recalling the coin, it teleports the maximum distance toward you and lands in an open space.

</column>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hellbreakers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers](/Sources.aspx?ID=307) pg. 213

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

---

This heavy metallic _+1 [bola](/Weapons.aspx?ID=433)_ is a favorite tool of rebels and rabble-rousers against armored opponents. Due to its weight, it has a range increment of 15 feet. When you successfully Strike a creature made of metal or wearing metal armor with this weapon, the bola attaches to the metal and the targeted creature takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speed until it spends an Interact action to remove the bola.

**Activate—Overcharge** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You overcharge the magnetic properties of the bola. You deal an extra 1d6 electricity damage with your next Strike with this weapon. On a hit, the target must also succeed at a DC 18 Reflex save or become [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1 round (or clumsy 2 on a critical failure), in addition to the normal effects. If the target is wearing metal armor, they take a –2 circumstance penalty to their save.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include a conductive metal.

fields.text: Item 3 Magnetic Bola May contain spoilers from Hellbreakers Uncommon Magical Source Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers pg. 213 Price 60 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 Base Weapon Bola This heavy metallic +1 bola is a favorite tool of rebels and rabble-rousers against armored opponents. Due to its weight, it has a range increment of 15 feet. When you successfully Strike a creature made of metal or wearing metal armor with this weapon, the bola attaches to the metal and the targeted creature takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speed until it spends an Interact action to remove the bola. Activate—Overcharge Single Action (electricity, manipulate, metal) Frequency once per day; Effect You overcharge the magnetic properties of the bola. You deal an extra 1d6 electricity damage with your next Strike with this weapon. On a hit, the target must also succeed at a DC 18 Reflex save or become clumsy 1 round (or clumsy 2 on a critical failure), in addition to the normal effects. If the target is wearing metal armor, they take a –2 circumstance penalty to their save. Craft Requirements The initial raw materials must include a conductive metal.

---

This collection of small magnets and metal rods comes in a wooden box. The magnets are strong enough to firmly cling to metal objects but too weak to move or suspend them. The metal rods are a quarter of an inch in diameter and vary in length from 3 to 6 inches. If connected with the magnets, these rods can be used to build flimsy shapes and structures, which collapse if external weight or pressure is applied.

    right="Item 5"

>
[Magnetic Shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1979)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Aura" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=206" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 64

**Price** 130 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Steel Shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Copper rings spiral around this [steel shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19). Twin electrical probes near the grip can socket into a jar of moderate (or higher leveled) [bottled lightning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3290), which takes 3 Interact actions to install.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** A bottled lightning is installed in the shield; **Effect** The shield becomes an electromagnet for 3 rounds. When an activated magnetic shield is raised, the circumstance bonus increases by 1 against attacks made with weapons primarily made of metal. If you use a [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) against a creature attacking you with such a weapon, you also gain a +1 item bonus to Disarm attempts against that weapon until the end of your next turn. The activation uses up the bottled lightning, and the shield can’t be activated again until a new one is installed.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Magnetic Suit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1117)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Aura" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=206" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 71

<row gap="medium">

**Duration** 10 minutes

**Usage** worn over armor and clothes

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This magnetized suit is strapped to your body over your armor or clothes. When you Activate it, you must choose whether to set it to attract or repel.

 While set to attract, you take a –1 status penalty to your AC against attacks made by metal weapons, while allies within a 10-foot emanation other than you gain a +1 status bonus to their AC. If set to repel, you gain a +1 status bonus to AC against attacks made with metal weapons. While attracting metal, you gain a +1 status bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) metal objects and [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) metal creatures and a –1 status penalty to Athletics checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) metal creatures. While repelling metal, you gain a +1 status bonus to Athletics checks to Shove metal creatures, but you take a –1 status penalty to Climb metal objects and Grapple metal creatures.

</column>

---

This magnetized suit is strapped to your body over your armor or clothes. When you Activate it, you must choose whether to set it to attract or repel.

While set to attract, you take a –1 status penalty to your AC against attacks made by metal weapons, while creatures within a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) for you and your allies gain a +1 status bonus to their AC. If set to repel, you gain a +1 status bonus to AC against attacks made with metal weapons. While repelling metal, you gain a +1 status bonus to Athletics checks to Shove metal creatures, but you take a –1 status penalty to Climb metal objects and Grapple metal creatures.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magnetite Scope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1213)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 181

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to firearm (scope)

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

More of a field projector than a scope, this small cylinder of magnetite has been enchanted to spread and accelerate the shrapnel of a [scatter](/Traits.aspx?ID=413) weapon further than the weapon's natural capabilities. Furthermore, some of the floating magnetite inside the scope's structure can help you when attempting to determine the your allies' locations. The magnetite scope grants you a +2 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=64) when using the scope to assist you in navigating. This scope can only be attached to firearms with the scatter trait.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The next Strike you make this round with the gun to which the scope is attached has its scatter radius increased by 5 feet.

</column>

The item bonus is +3, and activating the scope increases the scatter radius by 10 feet.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magnetizing](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1833)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 13

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto metal armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This rune alters the magnetic polarity of your armor, making other metal items drawn to it ever so slightly. You can amplify the magnetic power of the armor to keep another creature from getting away from you.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** A creature adjacent to you is made of metal or wearing metal armor; **Effect** You magnetize your armor. If you or the target attempt to move away from one another, treat each square as difficult terrain. This doesn't affect movement that keeps you the same distance from one another, so you could still Step if you remained adjacent to the target. This effect ends once either of you is no longer adjacent to the other at the end of an action.

 This Activation might work on some creatures partially made of metal, such as those with metal scales, as determined by the GM. Likewise, the GM might determine some metal creatures are non-magnetic, depending on the metal they're made of.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magnifying Glass of Elucidation](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1438)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 110

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The magnifying glass of elucidation is available for purchase for any common languages, as well as any other languages to which a PC has gained access._

**Price** 125 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These well-aged wooden magnifying glasses are engraved with a variety of runes. Each is imbued with a specific language. When you use a magnifying glass to examine writing of its imbued language, it translates the writing into a language you understand. For example, an elf who speaks only [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4) using a _magnifying glass of elucidation_ imbued with [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3) would see Dwarven writing as Elven when observed through the magnifying glass. The magnifying glass only provides direct translations and doesn't automatically allow you to understand codes or extremely esoteric passages—you still need to attempt a skill check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22).

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You scan up to two pages of writing with the _magnifying glass of elucidation_, imbuing the magnifying glass with the information you scanned. You can use a separate 3-action activity to have the magnifying glass reproduce the imbued information onto blank paper exactly as it appeared when you Activated the magnifying glass. The reproduction is a direct copy of the pages but doesn't imbue the reproduction with any magical effects or other special effects. As such, you can copy the writing of a scroll, for example, but it will only be mundane writing and not have any magical effect. The magnifying glass can only hold one instance of information at a given time; Activating the magnifying glass a second time or reproducing the information clears out the magnifying glass's information.

**Craft Requirements** You know the language imbued in the magnifying glass.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

These scopes use magically enhanced lenses to extend the range of your weapon and help spot distant foes. The scope grants you a +1 item bonus to visual Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) creatures through the scope.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** While gazing through the scope, you zoom in on your targets to make it easier to hit them at a distance. You increase the [range](/Rules.aspx?ID=2195) increment of the weapon to which the scope is attached by 5 feet until the beginning of your next turn or until you’re no longer wielding the weapon, whichever comes first.

**Bulk** 3

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This suit of _+2 resilient [splint mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=11)_ has a large, green gemstone inset in a prominent location.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You are hit or critically hit with an attack, but damage hasn’t been rolled yet;  **Effect** You force the attacker to reroll the attack roll and use the worse result. This effect has the [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) trait.

 Activating the armor causes the gemstone to turn gray and become inert. You cannot activate the armor again until the stone returns to its original green color. The gem turns green again after 1 week or when a significant foe critically succeeds at an attack roll targeting you. (If an enemy rolls a critical success at an attack against you and you force the attacker to reroll that critical success, that critical success does not recharge the mail of luck.) Even if the armor’s power returns before a week has elapsed, it can’t be activated more than once per day.

---

An aetheric irritant is a chime that can emit a subsonic frequency that otherworldly beings find unpleasant. When you Activate an aetheric irritant, you sound the chime and place it on the ground in a square within your reach. Creatures with the [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), or [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) traits must attempt a Will save when they enter the affected area and at the beginning of every turn they are in the affected area. Those who fail the save treat the area as difficult terrain until the beginning of their next turn. A creature that critically succeeds at the save is immune to all aetheric irritants for 24 hours. An aetheric irritant continues to hum until it shakes itself to pieces after 10 minutes of being activated or it is moved, whichever comes first.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 89

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>10 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This syrupy ink smells organic and faintly spoiled. It’s tied to one of Ushernacht’s engines, created with a sample of the fluid from inside the engine. If the associated engine stops functioning, all ink linked with it can no longer be activated, including freshly created ink.

When you write a question on a sheet of paper using the astonishing ink, handwriting scrawls over the paper after 10 minutes, answering with the knowledge it can draw from its engine. The astonishing ink has all Lore skills and attempts a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check to answer the question using the listed bonus. At the GM’s discretion, the astonishing ink takes a –4 circumstance penalty to the check if the question relates to advice, emotions, opinions, or other subjective topics.

If the astonishing ink fails (but not critically fails) the check to Recall Knowledge, the writing turns blood-red as it forms disturbing words. Anyone reading these words must succeed at a Will save at the listed DC or become [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 until they get a full night’s rest. The bloody message may also carry valuable or misleading information at the GM’s discretion.

You can use a vial of astonishing ink to ask 5 questions before it’s used up.

This small doll has been carved from a fragment of Bloodstone. When you Activate a _bloodstone doll_ in response to another’s magic, you Interact to take it in hand and hold it up toward the triggering creature. Attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) check against the triggering spell at the listed bonus and rank.

 If the spell would be counteracted, the _bloodstone doll_ instead influences the summoned creature. You gain control of the summoned creature and can dictate its 2 actions for that turn. The triggering creature then regains control of their summoned creature, but the summoned creature takes a –2 status penalty to attack rolls against you. Your _bloodstone doll_ shatters when the summon spell ends.

You pride yourself on being well prepared with weaponry for any situation. Your dark-gray boots might appear mundane, but you know that they can conjure a blade at any moment. Even the most thorough of searches can’t find a knife that doesn’t exist yet.

**Activate—Draw Secret Blade** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You reach down to your boot, draw a [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358) from it, and make a ranged or melee Strike with it. This dagger is created magically and does not exist before being drawn. The dagger remains a physical object until the next time you use Draw Secret Blade, and it disappears as a new blade is created.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 232

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This finely crafted, seemingly mundane parchment is useful for writing sensitive documents. When words are written on this parchment, they instantly scramble into unrecognizable script, requiring a DC 20 check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363). Both of the parchment’s activations require speaking a password or pass phrase, imbued into the parchment when created. A character must critically succeed on the check to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) when examining the parchment to learn the password. 

**Activate—Burn After Reading** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The words on the parchment seem to catch fire, completely burning away while leaving the parchment unharmed and ready to bear more text. 

**Activate—Decode Writing** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The scrambled words align into the originally written script.

**Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 222

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The damage type(s) for this item must be chosen at purchase or when crafted._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

---

This _[+2 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [longspear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=361)_ was crafted by a renowned monster hunter, who designed the prototype from the bones and scales of a [diabolic dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2939). The drathyrican folds of a young dragon, the organ that generates their magical breath, are crucial to the operation of the spear. The mechanics of the weapon are largely based on an [injection spear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=170): when the safety is disengaged and a secondary lever is squeezed, it produces a magical effect like a dragon’s breath from the hollow tip of the spear. 

**Activate—Breath of the Spear** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The dragon’s tongue releases a burst of energy that manifests as a 30-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) dealing 6d6 damage with a DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. You can’t use this activation again for 1d4 rounds. The damage type matches the breath of the dragon the weapon was made from, and this activation has the corresponding trait.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the drathyrican folds of a [dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=395).

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Golden Wings](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4959)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 50

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** 2
</row>

**Access** You're from Hermea

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pair of huge wings is crafted from numerous feathers made of a lightweight, golden magical alloy. When activated, the wings emit a melodic sound and a shimmering glow. 

**Activate—Assisted Flight** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For the next 10 minutes, you can [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) 20 feet, using the wings to propel yourself. You must land on a space with solid ground. For the duration, you also emit a [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 20-foot radius and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) for the next 20 feet. You take a –2 item penalty to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

pfs="Standard"

Golden Wings
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

pfs="Standard"

</traits>

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 50

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When you activate the wings, for the duration, you can also use an action to flap the wings to glide slowly toward the ground, 5 feet down and up to 20 feet forward through the air. As long as you spend 1 action gliding each round and haven’t yet reached the ground, you remain in the air at the end of your turn.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 9"
pfs="Standard"
>
Major Golden Wings
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 50

**Price** 650 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When you activate the wings, you also gain a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) of 20 feet for the duration.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 17"
pfs="Standard"
>
True Golden Wings
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 50

**Price** 14,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When you activate the wings, you also gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed or 25 feet, whichever is greater, for the duration.

<traits>

**Bulk** L

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Strike</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This flask contains a caustic irritant that makes a target’s skin, scales, or carapace extremely sensitive to further nicks and burns. An inflammation flask deals the listed acid damage and acid [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage. On a hit, the target also gains [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) to acid, fire, and slashing damage for 3 rounds. Many types of inflammation flask grant a bonus to attack rolls.

The target can end the weakness effect by three means: being drenched with water (such as submersion or exposure to an area [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) effect), being [Administered First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) (whose DC in based on the bomb type), or regaining Hit Points from a single effect equal to twice the inflammation flask’s level. A creature that critically fails to Administer First Aid in this way deals untyped damage to the target equal to the inflammation flask’s initial acid damage.

---

When you crack open this soft, spongy seedpod, you can use it as a [catalyst](/Rules.aspx?ID=1509) when casting a [_mist_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1606) spell. When you do, irritating pollen fills the area for the spell’s duration. Creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude saving throw at the listed DC to avoid sneezing uncontrollably. On a failed save, the creature gains the listed condition for the listed time. A creature that succeeds at this saving throw becomes temporarily immune to the irritating seedpod’s pollen for 10 minutes.

Your armor bathes your wounds in the cool light of the moon. While wearing this armor, whenever you would be healed by a spell or [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) effect, you recover an additional 2 Hit Points. You regain additional Hit Points from _moonweave_ only the first time you regain HP from a given [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) spell or effect, so a spell or effect that heals you repeatedly over a duration would restore additional Hit Points only once, when you’re first healed.

You can use this slimy, rotting mushroom as a [spell catalyst](/Rules.aspx?ID=1509) when you cast an [_acid grip_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1436) spell by tapping it against the target, causing the mushroom to release a cloud of necrotic spores. When you do, acid grip loses the [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) trait, gains the [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=614) trait, and all acid damage the spell deals becomes [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage. On a hit, the target additionally gains the [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) and [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) conditions, with the listed values, as the spores consume their flesh. As long as the target is taking [persistent void damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), they can’t reduce the value of their sickened condition below 1.

**Activate—Chained Grasp** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You successfully Strike with the _ouroboros flail_ as part of activating its _extending_ rune; **Requirements** ; **Effect** The head of the flail wraps around the target of the triggering Strike and drags it in your direction. The target must succeed at a DC 32 Fortitude save or be pulled adjacent to you. A creature pulled to you is then [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by the flail until the end of your next turn unless you move, your target [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 31), or you attack with the flail, whichever comes first. 

**Activate—Infinite Links** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You extend the flail’s chain, then wrap it across itself and strike two links together. This severs up to a 60-foot loop of usable chain from the flail, which instantly returns to its normal length. If you use Infinite Links again, any previous chain you created with it disappears after 1 round. As with most obviously magical and temporary constructs, the chain can’t be sold.

---

This innocuous little charm looks like nothing so much as a patch of coarse white or dark gray fur, usually made to resemble a lucky rabbit’s foot or something else. When you activate the talisman, the triggering attack gains the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) trait, and you fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), feigning death. An [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) surrounds you, causing you to appear dead for up to 1 minute. Any creature that touches the illusion or uses the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action to examine you can attempt to disbelieve the illusion. The DC to disbelieve the illusion is 18. Any action requiring you to move or make noise immediately ends the illusion.

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

---

This odd metal rod is often misinterpreted as a mechanical wand of some kind.

Any gadgeteer or mage will be able to elaborate on the fact that magic wands do not need to be throughly covered in a copper wire coil and that the pointed quartz crystal at its tip thrums with electricity, not magic. When activated, electricity courses through you, allowing you to move through the voltage that arcs through the air. You instantly transport yourself and any items you’re wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space up to 20 feet away that you can see. If this would bring another creature with you— even if you’re carrying it in an extradimensional container— the teleportation fails. You and all creatures in a line between your original location and your destination take 2 electricity damage.

[Sihedron Medallion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4043)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 69

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These amulets once served as tokens of loyalty between the runelords and their favored agents. Though they vary in appearance, they all share a common design—a leather or metallic cord attached to a metal disc inscribed with the seven-pointed star known as the Sihedron. For original _Sihedron medallions_ created before Earthfall, a runelord of old Thassilon (not a character with the runelord archetype) doesn’t reduce the DC of any [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1662) spell they cast against a creature that wears a Sihedron medallion even if they have never met the target or are unaware of the target’s identity. If such a runelord successfully scries on a creature wearing an original _Sihedron medallion_, they can use the wearer’s voice to issue messages to those in the vicinity. _Sihedron medallions_ created in more modern times don’t possess this disadvantage.

A dead body that wears a _Sihedron medallion_ doesn’t decay, and bugs or other pests (such as maggots) are prevented from consuming the remains, but unlike the effects of [_peaceful rest_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1625), this doesn’t offer any protection against undeath, nor does it have an impact on spells that require the corpse to have died within a certain amount of time. 

**Activate—Bolster Flesh** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your flesh is augmented with magical vitality. You gain 10 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) for 8 hours.

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>[Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306)</row></row>

---

This rare alchemical bomb gathers and concentrates the emotions that linger in a burial ground where generations of beloved ancestors have been interred, infusing that powerful emotional energy into the alchemically prepared powdered [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920) stored within the bomb. This energy glows with a soft, silver radiance and, if stored in a clear container, allows a silversoul bomb to be used as a [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2760) to illuminate an area.

A silversoul bomb grants an item bonus to attack rolls and deals mental damage plus additional effects, according to the bomb’s type. [Nindorus](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=353) are particularly harmed by silversoul bombs and take the listed persistent mental damage, according to the bomb’s type. Against nindorus, the bomb’s item bonus also applies to its save DC to resist being [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) or [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59). Creatures that have [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) to silver (including most nindorus) have an equal amount of weakness to the mental damage caused by a silversoul bomb, due to the silver infused into the energy within.

This energy glows with a soft, silver radiance and, if stored in a clear container, allows a silversoul bomb to be used as a torch to illuminate an area. A silversoul bomb grants an item bonus to attack rolls and deals mental damage plus additional effects, according to the bomb’s type. Nindorus are particularly harmed by silversoul bombs and take the listed persistent mental damage, according to the bomb’s type. Against nindorus, the bomb’s item bonus also applies to its save DC to resist being dazzled or blinded. Creatures that have weakness to silver (including most nindorus) have an equal amount of weakness to the mental damage caused by a silversoul bomb, due to the silver infused into the energy within. Item 3 Silversoul Bomb Source Season of Ghosts (Hardcover) pg. 296 Price 10 gp You gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls, and the bomb deals 2d4 mental damage, 1d6 persistent mental damage to nindorus, and 2 mental splash damage. A creature that takes splash damage from the bomb and fails a DC 17 Fortitude save is dazzled for 1 round as glowing silver particles cling to its face. Item 11 Greater Silversoul Bomb Source Season of Ghosts (Hardcover) pg. 296 Price 250 gp You gain a +2 item bonus to attack rolls, and the bomb deals 3d4 mental damage, 2d6 persistent mental damage to nindorus, and 3 mental splash damage. Item 17 Major Silversoul Bomb Source Season of Ghosts (Hardcover) pg. 296 Price 2,500 gp You gain a +3 item bonus to attack rolls, and the bomb deals 4d4 mental damage, 3d6 persistent mental damage to nindorus, and 4 mental splash damage. **Trigger** You are [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) at the beginning of your turn.

 
</row>

---

Carved from an [arboreal’s](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=364) knuckle, this wooden torus can be activated despite your being unconscious. The knot then sprouts several roots that arch over your body like a spider’s legs. These lift you a few inches off the ground before [Striding](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) and carrying you with them. The roots prioritize taking you away from obvious harm, though as a reaction, an ally who speaks [Arboreal](/Languages.aspx?ID=26) can command the roots to carry you to a particular point within range. 

After moving, the roots continue protecting you; this counts as [Raising a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316), giving you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the beginning of your next turn. The roots use the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction against the first physical attack against you, after which the roots crumble.

[Soldier's Syrup](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4002)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 80

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This thick syrup sweetens potions and creates a distinctive, metallic flavor associated with the festival days in Dhuraxilis. Partygoers are fond of mixing _soldier’s syrup_ with potions to extend their release.

Activating a dose of _soldier’s syrup_ requires you to combine it with another consumable potion that takes 1 action to activate. After swirling the mixture for a few moments, you must either imbibe the augmented potion within 1 minute, or the potion reverts to its unaugmented state. The potion’s level cannot exceed that of the _soldier’s syrup_ it is mixed with, otherwise the syrup is wasted.

When consumed, a _soldier’s syrup_–augmented potion does not immediately grant its benefits to you. Instead, you can activate the potion within the next hour as a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait. You can have only one _soldier’s syrup_–augmented potion consumed at a time; consuming a second one renders the first one inert. If you do not activate the potion within 1 hour, the potion spoils inside you, and you become [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 for 24 hours.

---

The Verduran Forest’s tiny tent-trap spider lays her eggs in a pyramidal web, and her young hatch only in response to intense vibration, such as the struggles of an ensnared insect or even songbird. Sadistic alchemists gather and augment these eggs, packing them in silken satchels that disgorge thousands of biting spider babies on impact. Many types of spider satchel grant a bonus to attack rolls. 

Until shaken off—or for the desperate target, incinerated—these spiders make it difficult to concentrate on anything other than escaping the swarm. The [fascination](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) effect ends automatically if a creature uses further [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=2251)s against the target, but hostile actions against the target’s allies don’t automatically end the effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 245

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When crafted, a _stampede medallion_ looks like nothing more than small silver disk, about the same size as a silver piece. When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny, bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon’s heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382). 

**Activate—Impossible Tide** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon momentarily manifests into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon’s Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

Activate—Impossible Tide Two Actions (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Effect Your eidolon momentarily manifests into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an emanation around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon’s Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 basic Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked prone. After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared. These shards of coalesced necromantic essence are sometimes found in the wake of an ancestor storm. Howling spirits are faintly visible, trapped inside the jagged, dark-green glass.

You can use the shard to cow the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) or briefly release the tormented souls from inside the glass. While you hold the stormshard, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks to [influence](/Rules.aspx?ID=1830) the undead. In addition, you can [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) undead creatures, even if those creatures are [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) or otherwise [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2313) to [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), or [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects.

Each creature in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) takes 4d8 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save). This small, opalescent stone glows with a light that constantly shifts between colors. When you activate the stone, you throw it into a space within 100 feet. The stone then casts [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69) on you and transports you to itself. This destroys the stone.

 You can instead hurl the stone at a creature in an attempt to bring that creature closer to you. Make a ranged Strike against a creature using your highest proficiency with a ranged weapon. The swapping stone has a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 15 feet. On a hit, the stone shatters against the creature, casting _dimension door_ on the creature and causing it to instantly teleport to a space adjacent to you. An unwilling creature can resist this teleportation with a successful DC 28 Will save.

fields.text: Item 1+ Tenderizer Grenade May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood Uncommon Acid Alchemical Bomb Consumable Plant Splash Source Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay pg. 77 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Single Action Strike Made from the acidic flesh of an especially astringent fruit found on the Plane of Wood, this bomb’s contents soften, oxidize, and season whatever they touch. Many types of this bomb grant an item bonus to attack rolls. On a successful Strike, a tenderizer grenade deals the listed acid damage to the target and the listed acid splash damage. Any resistances the target has against bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage are reduced by an amount based on the bomb’s type. In addition, the target is showered with appetizing esters, oils, and salts, making them off-guard against jaws Strikes, fangs Strikes, or similar Strikes with a creature’s mouth. These additional effects last until the end of your next turn, or for 1 minute on a critical hit. Item 1 Lesser Tenderizer Grenade Source Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay pg. 77 Price 4 gp The bomb deals 1d6 acid damage. Item 3 Moderate Tenderizer Grenade Source Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay pg. 77 Price 12 gp You gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 2d6 points of acid damage. Item 11 Greater Tenderizer Grenade Source Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay pg. 77 Price 275 gp You gain a +2 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 3d6 points of acid damage. Item 17 Major Tenderizer Grenade Source Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay pg. 77 Price 2,750 gp You gain a +3 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 4d6 points of acid damage.

This carved chunk of amber contains a single tuft of gray feathers, which spark with electricity to create an odd jittery sensation in anyone holding the amber for long. When used as part of a _[_thunderstrike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1721)_ spell, the _thunderbird tuft_ funnels electricity back into the spellcaster in a defensive nimbus. For 1 minute, any creature that touches you or that hits you with a melee unarmed attack or non-reach melee weapon attack takes the listed electricity damage.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 195

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +13; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** speech ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) and 1 imparted language)

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +13, [Nobility Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +13, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +13

**Int** +3, **Wis** +3, **Cha** +3

**Will** +14 

</column>

---        

Forged in platinum, a _majordomo torc_ is engraved with heraldic insignias along with one language's alphabet, much like a [_choker of elocution_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=422). You gain a +1 item bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) checks and the ability to understand, speak, and write the torc's language. Your excellent elocution reduces the DC of the flat check to perform an auditory action while [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) from 5 to 3.

 Upon being invested, the torc appoints itself your majordomo and, given the chance, takes over coordinating your social calendar, engagements, and wardrobe. A _majordomo torc_ has a prim, fussy disposition, and although it defers to you, it can grow sardonic if you frequently ignore its advice. The torc has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _majordomo torc_ casts [_befitting attire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=867) on you, usually to your specifications. However the torc can also choose the appearance of the illusion for you.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

As you move your body, qi flows into _mala beads of foresight_ you wear and have invested, making them one with your life force. **Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) monk qi spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

You're affected by an [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=15) spell.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [monk](/Classes.aspx?ID=8) with divine qi spells.

>
[Malefic Mirror](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3590)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
<trait label="Scrying" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=689" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 107

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This magic mirror is the conduit between the mirror seer and the source of their power. Any creature who looks in this silver mirror can speak with the entity the mirror is linked to, but only a creature who has made a pact with the entity can activate the _malefic mirror_. If the mirror is shattered, any spells created by the mirror end (it has AC 5, object immunities, Hardness 5, HP 20, and BT 10).

**Activate—Peer Beyond** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662))    **Effect** The mirror casts a DC 28 [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1662) spell for the benefit of the creature activating it. The target must be within the owner's domain (typically within 20 miles of the mirror). The viewer's familiarity with the target doesn't affect the spell's DC. 

**Activate—Mirror Mimicry** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662))    **Effect** The mirror transforms its owner's appearance into an exact copy of any [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) the owner desires, with a pale mimicry of that creature's abilities. This has the effects of a 3rd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) spell with a duration of 4 hours. The activation can also be Dismissed.

 In addition, the disguised creature can automatically create illusions to mimic the abilities of the subject, with the appearance of spells, abilities, or even impressive physical deeds. These deeds are entirely illusory and can be disbelieved with a successful DC 28 Perception check. If an illusion makes it appear as though the creature moved farther or differently than they actually can (such as making them fly or teleport), the actual creature turns [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), and their illusory image persists until the end of the creature's next turn. If the creature and their illusory self aren't in the same space at that point, the activation ends, revealing the deception.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Malleable Clay](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1522)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley](/Sources.aspx?ID=113) pg. 80

**Price** 30 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You Strike with the affixed weapon

**Requirement** You're trained in the affixed weapon.
</row>

</column>

---

This small lump of clay is malleable and can be molded into innumerable shapes and forms. When affixed, the clay takes on the appearance of the affixed weapon. When activated, the affixed weapon gains the [versatile](/Traits.aspx?ID=200) bludgeoning, versatile piercing, and versatile slashing weapon traits for the triggering Strike and all other attacks for 1 minute. With each attack, the clay changes shape, taking on the appearance of a different weapon that deals damage of the chosen damage type.

</column>

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 100 **Price** 990 gp **Usage** worn armor **Bulk** 2 **Base Armor** [Scale Mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=45) --- The faint glow beneath the thick, algae-green scales of this suit of _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2785) [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) [scale mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=45)_ hints at the armor’s source. **Activate—Luminous Lure** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The _mamlambo scale_ sheds [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) in a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). The light has a duration of 1 minute, but you can extinguish the light with an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action. A creature that begins its turn in the light must attempt a DC 26 Will save. Regardless of the save’s result, the creature is temporarily immune for 1 hour. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72), and for as long as it remains in the light, it must spend at least 1 of its actions on each of its turns to move closer to the source of the light. If the creature ends its movement adjacent to you, it is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 until it is out of the light or until you make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against it.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature is also [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the first Strike you make against it while it is slowed. **Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the scales and hide of a [mamlambo](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1439).

This heavy, 12-foot-tall _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [composite longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=74)_ is fashioned from mammoth tusks lashed together. Due to its great size, you can attack with the _Mammoth Bow_ only if you're Large or larger. The _Mammoth Bow_ deals 2d6 additional piercing damage because of its incredible, magically enhanced draw power. Additionally, the Mammoth Bow has a 180-foot [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) instead of a 100-foot range increment, but its [volley](/Traits.aspx?ID=201) range increases from 30 feet to 50 feet.

fields.text: Item 12 Mammoth Bow May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame Unique Evocation Magical Source Pathfinder #177: Burning Tundra pg. 74 Price 2,000 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 4 Base Weapon Composite Longbow This heavy, 12-foot-tall +2 striking composite longbow is fashioned from mammoth tusks lashed together. Due to its great size, you can attack with the Mammoth Bow only if you're Large or larger. The Mammoth Bow deals 2d6 additional piercing damage because of its incredible, magically enhanced draw power. Additionally, the Mammoth Bow has a 180-foot range increment instead of a 100-foot range increment, but its volley range increases from 30 feet to 50 feet.

---

This impressive-looking weapon is forged from a single piece of cold iron. _Man-Feller_ is a _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=16)_ that strikes particularly painful wounds into the flesh of [humans](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6) it hews. The battle axe deals an additional 1d6 slashing damage to any human it wounds. This benefit doesn't apply against humans disguised as other creatures. It's up to GM discretion whether this effect applies against such a disguised human.

 Those who might find it amusing to point out the awkward and almost comedic duplication in the weapon's name would do well to consider that those who previously mocked the name of King Merlokrep's favorite axe to the kobold's face didn't live long enough to finish their self-congratulatory chuckles.

According to reports, as well as Emelett's own marketing pitches, this lotion is derived from rare mana rattlesnakes whose oils ward against poison and disease. When applied, you can attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) a [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) or [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) effect currently afflicting you. The potion has a counteract level of 5 and a +15 modifier for the roll. You also acquire a serpentine appearance, growing fangs and scaly skin. For 1 hour, you gain a fangs [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage plus 1 poison damage.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 288

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You can manacle someone who is willing or otherwise at your mercy as an exploration activity taking 10–30 seconds depending on the creature's size and how many manacles you apply. A two-legged creature with its legs bound takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds, and a two-handed creature with its wrists bound has to succeed at a DC 5 flat check any time it uses a manipulate action or else that action fails. This DC may be higher depending on how tightly the manacles constrain the hands. A creature bound to a stationary object is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24). For creatures with more or fewer limbs, the GM determines what effect manacles have, if any. Freeing a creature from poor manacles requires two successful DC 17 Thievery checks, simple manacles requires three successes at DC 22, average manacles require four successes at DC 27, good manacles require five successes at DC 32, and superior manacles require six successes at DC 42.

A two-legged creature with its legs bound takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds, and a two-handed creature with its wrists bound has to succeed at a DC 5 flat check any time it uses a manipulate action or else that action fails. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Manacles of Persuasion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=569)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Nonlethal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=188" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 122

**Price** 45 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn on wrists

**Bulk** 1
</row>

**Access** follower of Zon-Kuthon

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These sturdy, [average manacles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=32) are connected by a thick iron chain that is much heavier than its appearance suggests at a glance. Followers of [Zon-Kuthon](/Deities.aspx?ID=20) sometimes employ _manacles of persuasion_ against captured enemies and spies. When the manacles are locked around an [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) creature’s wrists, they begin to sap the life out of the victim, dealing 2 negative damage per hour until the creature falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38). The effect is [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), so the damage doesn’t cause the creature to become [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11). While the creature is unconscious, the manacles deal no damage and allow the creature to recover Hit Points normally to a maximum of 10 Hit Points, at which point the manacles begin to deal damage once more. The manacles have no effect on a creature that is not immobilized.

</title>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />

These stylized red gloves are constructed from plates of leather that have been treated to resemble insect chitin. The gloves grant the wearer a +2 item bonus to Athletics checks to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) or [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380).

**Activate—Crushing Embrace** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** You are grappling a creature; **Effect** You Strike the creature you are grappling with a melee weapon or unarmed attack. This Strike deals an additional 3d6 precision damage and gains the death trait. The body of a creature that is slain by Crushing Embrace is so gruesomely damaged that the creature's body cannot be affected by any effect that requires an intact body to function, such as the [_talking corpse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1712) spell.

    level="1"

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mantle of Amazing Health](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2140)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 104

**Price** 40,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ragged cloak doesn't appear to be anything special at first glance, seemingly made from mangy black bear fur with various rings of blackened iron piercing the edge of the skin. While somewhat off-putting, the mantle grants a +2 status bonus to all Fortitude saving throws against [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) and [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126). When you invest the mantle, you either increase your Constitution modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever is higher.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per round; **Trigger** You take damage;  **Effect** Drawing the cloak around you, you reduce the damage taken by 10.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** If you're currently afflicted by a poison or a disease, you can hold the cloak tight to your body and immediately attempt a saving throw to end the effect. If that saving throw succeeds, you end the effect of either the poison or disease no matter the stage of the affliction. Furthermore, you gain immunity to that poison or disease for 24 hours.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    right="Item 3"

>
[Mantle of Far Horizons](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5219)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 143

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _mantle of far horizons_ helps to bring comfort and a sense of security while traveling, filling you with confidence and bolstering your energy during long journeys. In areas where you can see the horizon, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks made to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=2406).

**Activate—Gaze upon the Horizon** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You raise the mantle's hood to augment your ability to see over large distances or through adverse weather. For the next hour, or until you lower your hood (whichever comes first), you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks made to observe things more than 500 feet away, or while in [weather](/Traits.aspx?ID=464)-related conditions that penalize your Perception checks (such as [fog](/Rules.aspx?ID=815) or [precipitation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2816)).

**Activate—Listen to the World** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You lower the mantle's hood to focus on the world's natural sounds rather than other distractions. For the next minute, or until you raise the mantle's hood (whichever comes first), you gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) effects.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
