---

This long, golden cloak is among the royal regalia of the emperors of Taldor. It was fashioned from the pelt of [Grogrisant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1727) itself, after being slain by Taldaris, and Grogrisant's mane was fashioned into a thick fringe that runs all along the mantle's edges. The paws of the Grogrisant cross beneath the wearer's throat, giving you an imposing appearance. The _Mantle of the Grogrisant_ grants you [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) resistance 15 and physical resistance 5 (except bludgeoning).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision, Interact ([evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pull the hood of the mantle over your face, revealing the six eyes of Grogrisant. The mantle gives off a flash of blinding light in a 60-foot emanation. All enemies within this area must attempt a DC 38 Fortitude saving throw. On a failure, they're [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 minute. On a critical failure, they're permanently blinded.

Activate—Illusory Thrash Two Actions (concentrate, illusion, manipulate, mental) Frequency once per day; Effect You wrap the mantle around your body, causing you to briefly appear much larger than you are. Make a melee Strike. This Strike deals an additional 4d6 mental damage. Craft Requirements The initial raw materials must include the hide of a tikbalang.

These tiny round balls are made of polished stone and colorful glass, and come in a bag of 200. You can pour marbles in an empty square adjacent to you with an Interact action. The first creature that moves into that square must succeed at a DC 13 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check or Reflex save (its choice) or fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). Once a creature enters a space with marbles, enough marbles are scattered that other creatures moving into that space don't need to attempt a roll to avoid falling.

Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49). By spending 1 minute to measure the height of the stars and planets, a holder who knows the time and date can determine the latitude, and a holder who knows their latitude can determine the date and time. An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies. A standard astrolabe functions only on steady ground.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 78

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Pathfinder Society does not use vehicle rules_

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** You're from the Mordant Spire

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The swirls on this wooden mask—often worn by Mordant Censors—move and shift, reflecting the shape of the nearest currents. Wearing the mask grants you a +1 item bonus to [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) and [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks. In addition, it allows you to pilot a boat with simply a thought. When you pilot a vehicle, you can keep both hands free and [Drive](/Actions.aspx?ID=3517) from any location on the vehicle. 

**Activate—Set the Course** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You are aboard a vehicle; **Effect** You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 minute or until you leave the vehicle, whichever comes first, and can use the extra action to [Take Control](/Actions.aspx?ID=3520) of the vehicle or, if you’re already piloting it, Drive or [Stop](/Actions.aspx?ID=3519) the vehicle.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mark Of The Torrent](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5252)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 177

**Price** 135 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** You’re a member of the Order of the Torrent.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The Order of the Torrent works to rescue kidnapped people, and their cobalt blue badge can often open doors that would otherwise be closed. When wearing this badge, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) or Gather Information about a missing person. 

**Activate—Modus Operandi** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** A kidnapping occurred within 15 feet of your location, or you have some information about the target or perpetrators of a kidnapping; **Effect** You attempt to Recall Knowledge about those who perpetrated the kidnapping, the information supernaturally surfacing in your mind. The GM determines what skill and DC to use for this check based on the level and nature of the perpetrators (usually a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) check at a standard DC for the perpetrator’s level). In addition, if you fail to Recall Knowledge about the kidnapper (but don’t critically fail), you eliminate one false lead about the kidnapper or how they abducted the target. For instance, you might determine that an incorporeal undead wasn’t involved, though you gain no other information about what happened. The mark can’t provide specific identifying information about the perpetrators, like their name or location.

</column>

---

A standard deck of cards consists of 54 cards made from thick paper contained within a paper sleeve. The most common deck used for games and gambling is known as the Old Mage deck and features four suits themed with the four essences of magic, each with 13 cards, as well as two wildcards. The name and appearance of the deck varies from region to region, such as the Magician's Deck in Taldor or the Deck of Masks in the Shackles.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 0"
pfs="Standard"
>
Marked Playing Cards
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

**Price** 1 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

</row>

</column>

---

A deck of marked playing cards appears to be an ordinary deck upon initial inspection but bears specific folds, colors, scratches, or other markings on each card that allow an informed user to know what's on the other side of a card. A deck of marked cards grants you a +1 item bonus to [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks or other relevant checks to gamble with the cards. You can determine that an unattended deck of cards is marked with a successful DC 20 Perception check. Determining that a deck is marked during play is more difficult and is typically determined by a Perception check against the dealer's Games Lore or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 299 **Price** 3 gp --- This snare is often used to mark intruders for later tracking or identification. When you create this snare, you must decide whether to make it a dye or a scent marker. Either type of marking grants a +2 circumstance bonus to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) the creature for up to 24 hours or until the dye or scent is washed off (requiring at least a gallon of water and 10 minutes of scrubbing). A creature that enters a square of the snare must attempt a DC 17 Reflex save. **Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The snare marks the creature.
**Critical Failure** The snare marks the creature, and the creature is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) until the end of its next turn.

This short, thick, stick-like object is crafted of wood and steel. Precious metals decorate the grip, and fine filigree marks the caps on each end. A _marshal’s baton_ grants you a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks against troops, individual soldiers, and military leaders.

**Activate—Stentorian Order** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You issue a command in a booming voice while gesturing with the _marshal’s baton_ and cast a [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470) spell (DC 18). This spell affects [troops](/Rules.aspx?ID=3364) and [swarms](/Traits.aspx?ID=707) as if they were a single creature.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs=""
>
[Martyr's Shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3126)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=636" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 305

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Steel Shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +12; precise vision 30 feet, imprecise hearing 30 feet

**Communication** speech ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) and [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115))

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +15, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +13

**Int** +0, **Wis** +2, **Cha** +4

**Will** +15 

</column>

---        

_A martyr's shield_ is a [_lesser sturdy shield_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=327) imbued with the compassion of a devout champion of a righteous deity, like [Iomedae](/Deities.aspx?ID=9) or [Vildeis](/Deities.aspx?ID=130), who sacrificed themself to save an ally. In addition to good-naturedly attempting to convert you to its religion, the _martyr's shield_ can use 1 reaction each round that, when raised, it uses to [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) to protect an ally adjacent to you. This follows the rules for Shield Block, but protects your ally instead. The _martyr's shield_ uses this reaction whether you would prefer it did so or not. The _martyr's shield_ can be upgraded to a stronger form of _sturdy shield_ by paying the difference in cost between its current type of _sturdy shield_ and the new type.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

---

This silvery _[minor reinforcing](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2811) [steel shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19)_ (Hardness 8, HP 64, and BT 32) bears the image of two soldiers standing side-by-side.

**Activate—Self Sacrifice** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Trigger** An ally within 20 feet of you would take physical damage; **Requirements** The _martyr's shield_ is raised; **Effect** When you activate this shield, it magically imposes itself in front of the triggering ally and takes the damage for them with the effects of [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212). Any damage that isn't prevented by the shield is transferred onto you.

A _martyr’s shield_ is a [_lesser sturdy shield_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=327) imbued with the compassion of a devout champion of a righteous deity, like [Iomedae](/Deities.aspx?ID=9) or [Vildeis](/Deities.aspx?ID=130), who sacrificed themself to save an ally.     level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Marvelous Calliope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=587)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God](/Sources.aspx?ID=23) pg. 74

**Price** 100 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This large slide whistle appears to be made of fine brass, the sides of which are engraved with musical notes and dancing clowns.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (command, envision, Interact);     **Effect** You blow a tune upon the slide whistle, causing the whistle to expand. The whistle sprouts from one into several, and then creates a large wooden frame and keyboard. By the time the unfolding is complete, the whistle fully transforms into a calliope, a wagon-sized contraption consisting of several steam whistles played like an organ. The calliope is heavy and anchored in place.

 You have a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play the calliope. The calliope has a tendency to produce music for a few seconds after you cease playing it, adding a jaunty and overlong conclusion to your music.

 If you use an Interact action to pull the small metal ring on the underside of the _marvelous calliope_, the calliope collapses back down into a slide whistle.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You play the calliope, causing it to cast [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34) on one of the listeners.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This set of [healer’s tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25) contains a seemingly endless supply of bandages, herbs, and healing items of impeccable quality, granting you a +2 item bonus to Medicine checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Treat Poison or 8 hours (Treat Disease);     **Effect** You can activate the tools when you use them to Treat Poison in order to produce the effects of [_neutralize poison_](/Spells.aspx?ID=207), or when you Treat Disease in order to produce the effects of [_remove disease_](/Spells.aspx?ID=251). <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 1+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Marvelous Miniature](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3002)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Expandable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=475" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 268

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Every _marvelous miniature_ is an exceptionally small replica of a real creature or object. The miniature is made from wood, pewter, or other simple materials, and features a rune etched into the underside of the replica's base. _Marvelous miniatures_ sometimes come packaged together; for example, the camping set features the boat, campfire, and horse miniatures. Activating a _marvelous miniature_ causes it to transform into another creature or object, which then can be used as normal for that object. Each miniature can be activated only once, with most of them permanently becoming the item in their description.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 8"
pfs="Standard"
>
Marvelous Miniature (Boat)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 268

**Price** 76 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This miniature can be activated only when tossed into a large body of water, such as a lake or broad river. It transforms into a [cutter](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=41). The cutter lasts 1 day.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 1"
pfs="Standard"
>
Marvelous Miniature (Campfire)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 268

**Price** 1 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When activated, this miniature transforms into an active campfire. The campfire doesn't require attending and remains fully lit for 8 hours, though it can be quenched as any other campfire.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Marvelous Miniature (Chest)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 268

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When you use this miniature, a small wooden chest appears and immediately opens. This chest can hold up to 10 Bulk worth of items. Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. fields.text: Item 1+ Marvelous Miniature Consumable Expandable Magical Source GM Core pg. 268 Usage held in 1 hand Activate Single Action (manipulate) Every marvelous miniature is an exceptionally small replica of a real creature or object. The miniature is made from wood, pewter, or other simple materials, and features a rune etched into the underside of the replica's base. Marvelous miniatures sometimes come packaged together; for example, the camping set features the boat, campfire, and horse miniatures. Activating a marvelous miniature causes it to transform into another creature or object, which then can be used as normal for that object. Each miniature can be activated only once, with most of them permanently becoming the item in their description. Item 8 Marvelous Miniature (Boat) Source GM Core pg. 268 Price 76 gp This miniature can be activated only when tossed into a large body of water, such as a lake or broad river. It transforms into a cutter. The cutter lasts 1 day. Item 1 Marvelous Miniature (Campfire) Source GM Core pg. 268 Price 1 gp When activated, this miniature transforms into an active campfire. The campfire doesn't require attending and remains fully lit for 8 hours, though it can be quenched as any other campfire. Item 3 Marvelous Miniature (Chest) Source GM Core pg. 268 Price 10 gp When you use this miniature, a small wooden chest appears and immediately opens. This chest can hold up to 10 Bulk worth of items. Once the chest is closed, it transforms again—this time into a key—taking all of the stored items with it. You can activate this key by spending an Interact action to turn it in an imaginary lock, which causes it to transform back into a chest with all of the items still inside. Once it has turned into a chest a second time, it forever remains a wooden chest. Item 4 Marvelous Miniature (Horse) Source GM Core pg. 268 Price 13 gp When activated, this miniature transforms into a horse. The horse can't attack or use reactions, but otherwise uses all the statistics of a riding horse and follows your basic commands. The horse doesn't need to eat or drink. After 8 hours, it reverts back to miniature form, then crumbles to dust. Item 1 Marvelous Miniature (Ladder) Source GM Core pg. 268 Price 3 gp When activated, this miniature transforms permanently into a 20-foot-long wooden ladder. Item 2 Marvelous Miniature (Swift Sparrow) May contain spoilers from Hellbreakers Uncommon Source Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers pg. 210 Price 6 gp Usage held in 1 hand When activated, this miniature transforms into a seemingly mundane sparrow. The sparrow flies to a destination of your choice within 200 feet that you can see, then Seeks in a 30-foot burst using your Perception modifier before returning. The sparrow then unravels into a small map of the area it perceived, including any creatures it saw. The map is rudimentary and doesn't reveal anything the sparrow failed to perceive.

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 97 **Price** 325 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**10 minutes (envision, Interact) --- _Marvelous pigment_ comes in a small container of shifting, multicolored paint that can magically create an object painted with it. The pigment is applied with a stick tipped with bristles, hair, or fur. The paint flows as you Activate the marvelous pigment and changes color at your whim as you paint. The paint can cover a 10-foot-square, two-dimensional surface. When you’re done painting, attempt a DC 30 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check. **Critical Success** The object you painted emerges from the surface as a real, permanent object no larger than 10 feet in any dimension. It’s non-magical and inanimate and has no value except to certain art collectors. If you paint a creature, machine, or form of energy (such as a campfire), these depictions appear only as inanimate sculptures. The created object has a painterly appearance that clearly marks its unusual origin, but is as real as any other.
**Success** As critical success, but the object constantly sheds flakes of paint until it falls apart, destroyed, after 24 hours.
**Failure** The pigments leave a painting that doesn’t quite look right and doesn’t become an object.
**Critical Failure** Is it a dog? Whatever you made is a pretty lousy painting and doesn’t resemble what you set out to make.

This stylized bird mask is equipped with a basic filter. The plague mask attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) any [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) or airborne diseases each round you breathe. The same replacement filters used in [water purifiers](/Equipment.aspx?ID=877) can be used with a plague mask, granting you the counteract modifier and effects of the filter for 20 minutes. Plague masks are uncommon items because the filters they use to protect from inhaled poisons and diseases are themselves uncommon. As such, you can buy a plague mask without a filter as a common item, though it's usually more cost-effective to buy a fine mask in the shape of a plague mask in that case.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 186 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn mask **Bulk** L --- This mask appears to be a pool of mirrored, shifting silver adhered to a thin metal plate. When you place it against your face, it melds to the shape of your head. The material is breathable and light, and does not obscure vision. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks while wearing the mask. When you invest the mask, you either increase your Charisma score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. **Activate** envision ([visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You attempt a Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance check; **Effect** You gain a +4 status bonus to the triggering check. This ability has no effect if you're under the effects of a disguise that hides the _mask of allure_. Depending on the skill used, the mirrored silver transforms into one of the following appearances.
  • **Deception** A swirl of silver, which entirely obscures and conceals your normal features.
  • **Diplomacy** A kind, gentle and inviting expression.
  • **Intimidation** A monstrous visage that shocks viewers into paying attention.
  • **Performance** A jovial humanoid face, the mouth cracked wide with a comedic smile or a tragic frown, depending on the nature of the performance.

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 80

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This mask’s features shift between various nonhuman elements, with each version reveling in grotesque and monstrous variations. During the festivals in Dhuraxilis, these masks are worn by influential and rich humans (or human-appearing populations) to better blend in with the monstrous crowds as they join in the revelry. While wearing the mask, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks.

**Activate—Monstrosity Meld** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You take on the general appearance of a type of non-humanoid creature that you can see, with the transformation lasting for 8 hours. Activating this effect doesn’t change your traits or statistics, nor does it grant any of the special abilities of the creature you’re imitating. It does not change your size, so a Medium creature that assumes the shape of a manticore remains Medium sized. This effect uses the same rules as the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) activity of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38). Onlookers always assume you’re the chosen type of creature unless they’re actively Seeking. You gain a +4 item bonus to your Deception DC against such Perception checks and add your level even if untrained.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 155, [Pathfinder #169: Kindled Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=94) pg. 74 **Price** 475 gp **Usage** worn mask --- A _mask of the cursed eye_ is decorated with at least one wide, staring eye. The first time each day you’re targeted with a detection, prediction, revelation, or scrying spell by a creature on your plane that you can’t perceive, the creature targeting you must attempt a DC 24 Will save. This effect is automatic and does not require you to Activate the item. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is unaffected, but you know you’ve been targeted with a spell that has one of these traits.
**Failure** The creature is [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 minute. You know you’ve been targeted with a spell that has one of these traits.
**Critical Failure** The creature is sickened 2 and dazzled for 10 minutes, and the spell is [disrupted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236). You gain a brief mental glimpse of the triggering creature and learn its approximate distance and direction.

[Mask of the Mantis](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3497)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Prey for Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 104

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn head

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The traditional headwear for the Red Mantis assassin is the _mask of the mantis_. Most of these masks are constructed from hard leather helmets that serve to obscure the assassin's identity and give them the appearance of possessing a mantis's head. Some variants, however, consist only of the mask itself, and are meant to be worn over the face. Regardless of the shape and style, all _masks of the mantis_ function the same.

 Members of the Vernai can use any mask of the mantis to enhance their frightening presence—something they often do simply to reveal their standing in the society without speaking a word, as detailed fully in the entry for Vernai's Ire activation below.

 While wearing a _mask of the mantis_, you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks.

**Activate—Enhance Vision** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast either [_darkvision_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1481) or [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) on yourself.

**Activate—Vernai's Ire** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))   **Requirements** You are a member of the Vernai; **Effect** You cause the mask of the mantis's eyes to shimmer with crimson light, granting yourself a far more harrowing visage. This light creates illumination equivalent to that of a candle. You can use this ability again to extinguish the frightening glow, but as long as Vernai's Ire remains active, you gain a +1 item bonus to Intimidation checks.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mask of Uncanny Breath](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2326)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 150

**Price** 1,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A thin wooden mask carved in the shape of a skull, monstrous face, or eerily featureless visage, a mask of uncanny breath fully covers your face. While wearing it, each breath you take feels cool and pure, perfectly flowing to feed your qi. You gain resistance 10 to [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) and can breathe in an airless or toxic environment. When you breathe in, fragments of bizarre knowledge flow through you, granting you a +2 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast an [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) monk qi spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strike hits a creature that breathes;  **Effect** The mask contorts and inhales, sucking breath from your target's lungs. The target falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) but doesn't fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) or drop what it's holding. It wakes up at the end of your turn if it hasn't been woken up already.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [monk](/Classes.aspx?ID=8) with occult qi spells.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Master Magus Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2327)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 150

**Price** 1,250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Elegant jewelry such as the _master magus ring_ adorns experienced [magi](/Classes.aspx?ID=17). Each ring has a significant metal and symbol to represent a particular hybrid study, such as a heavy iron ring with an icon of a mountain for [inexorable iron](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=1), or glittering silver with a shield-like emblem for [sparkling targe](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=3). You gain a +2 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a magus conflux spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The ring transports you and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space you can see within a range equal to your Speed. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) container—the activation fails and is used.

**Craft Requirements** You are a magus.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7+"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Mat of Resilience](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3745)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #209: Destroyer's Doom](/Sources.aspx?ID=251) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** placed on a surface

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This light but sturdy woven mat, a miniature version of the floating foundations used in villages of the Dirt Sea, is carried tied in a tight roll. When you use an action to unfurl the mat onto an unoccupied horizontal space, the mat covers the existing terrain to create a smooth surface that can be walked on as if it were solid ground. [Difficult](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) or [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2368) in that square may be treated as normal while the mat of resilience covers it. The mat can be rolled back up or moved to an adjacent square using an Interact action, but it cannot be moved or put away while a creature is atop it. 

**Activate—Steady Ground** <actions string="Single Action" /> (envision)    **Effect** You unfurl the mat and choose which shape it takes, either a 10-foot square or a 20-foot by 5-foot [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388).

**Activate—Sturdy Foundation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** A creature is atop the mat; **Effect** The creature enters a simple stance that makes the most of the mat’s stabilizing magic. While in this stance, if at least half of the creature’s space is atop the mat, it cannot gain the [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) condition.

</column>

fields.text: Item 7+ Mat of Resilience May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk Uncommon Magical Source Pathfinder #209: Destroyer's Doom pg. 83 Usage placed on a surface Bulk 1 This light but sturdy woven mat, a miniature version of the floating foundations used in villages of the Dirt Sea, is carried tied in a tight roll. When you use an action to unfurl the mat onto an unoccupied horizontal space, the mat covers the existing terrain to create a smooth surface that can be walked on as if it were solid ground. Difficult or hazardous terrain in that square may be treated as normal while the mat of resilience covers it. The mat can be rolled back up or moved to an adjacent square using an Interact action, but it cannot be moved or put away while a creature is atop it. Activate—Steady Ground Single Action (envision) Effect You unfurl the mat and choose which shape it takes, either a 10-foot square or a 20-foot by 5-foot line. Activate—Sturdy Foundation Single Action (manipulate) Requirements A creature is atop the mat; Effect The creature enters a simple stance that makes the most of the mat’s stabilizing magic. While in this stance, if at least half of the creature’s space is atop the mat, it cannot gain the off-guard condition. Item 7 Mat of Resilence Source Pathfinder #209: Destroyer's Doom pg. 83 Price 330 gp Item 12 Greater Mat of Resilence Source Pathfinder #209: Destroyer's Doom pg. 83 Price 1,800 gp The mat’s surfaces increase to a 20-foot square and a 40- foot by 5-foot line.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs=""
>
[Matsuki's Medicinal Wine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2685)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Drug" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=261" />
<trait label="Ingested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 82

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Old Matsuki's private brew has quite the kick. In addition to making you tipsy, this medicinal wine works wonders in helping to recover from disease—including (ironically) drug addiction. Matsuki's medicinal wine functions as [alcohol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=622), except that its saving throw is a DC 18 Fortitude save. In addition, upon drinking a dose of Matsuki's medicinal wine, you gain a +2 item bonus to Fortitude saving throws against [diseases](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) and [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) for 24 hours. This applies to your daily save against a disease's progression; however, the bonus doesn't apply to any checks you attempt against Matsuki's medical wine itself.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

In addition to making you tipsy, this medicinal wine works wonders in helping to recover from disease. When you drink a dose of this wine you must succeed at a DC 18 Fortitude save to avoid becoming off-guard for 10 minutes (and also clumsy 1 for this duration if you critically fail the saving throw). Regardless of the saving throw’s results, you gain a +2 item bonus to Fortitude saving throws against diseases and poisons for the next 24 hours. This applies to your daily save against a disease’s progression as well.

[Mattock of the Titans](/Equipment.aspx?ID=391)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 601

**Price** 36,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 16
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Greatpick](/Weapons.aspx?ID=23)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This 15-foot-long [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374) digging tool is far too big for even a Large creature to wield, though if you’re a Small or larger creature, you can wield it while wearing a [_belt of giant strength_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=398), as though it were appropriately sized for you and had 2 Bulk. The GM might also allow you to wield the mattock if you have some other means of wielding oversized weapons, such as if you’re a Large barbarian with the [giant instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=4) or are a Huge creature. When it’s used as a weapon, the _mattock of the titans_ has the statistics of a _+3 greater striking [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=300) adamantine [greatpick](/Weapons.aspx?ID=23)_.

 While you’re wielding the _mattock of the titans_, you gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks. You can use it to loosen or push soft earth at a rate of 1 minute per 5-foot cube or smash through solid stone at the rate of 5 minutes per 5-foot-cube.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You dig furiously with the mattock to non-magically replicate the effects of an [_earthquake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=95) spell.

**Craft Requirements** You are a titan, and the initial raw materials must include 8,100 gp of adamantine.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 88

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Powered by electricity, you can turn a mechanical torch on and off by toggling a lever on the torch with an Interact action. When active, the torch sheds bright light in either a 20-foot radius (and dim light to the next 40 feet) or a 40-foot cone (and dim light to the next 40 feet). Changing this area requires a single Interact action to flip a switch. The torch carries sufficient charge to operate for ten minutes. You can recharge the torch in 1 minute via an integrated crank-charging mechanism, turning the clockwork gears and generating sparks to power the torch, though doing so requires two hands.

fields.text: Item 1 Mechanical Torch Clockwork Source Guns & Gears pg. 88 PFS Note All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book Price 10 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Powered by electricity, you can turn a mechanical torch on and off by toggling a lever on the torch with an Interact action. When active, the torch sheds bright light in either a 20-foot radius (and dim light to the next 40 feet) or a 40‑foot cone (and dim light to the next 40 feet). Changing this area requires a single Interact action to flip a switch. The torch carries sufficient charge to operate for ten minutes. You can recharge the torch in 1 minute via an integrated crank-charging mechanism, turning the clockwork gears and generating sparks to power the torch, though doing so requires two hands.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magical Medals](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3971)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Military leaders or heads of state award these special medals to commend exemplary performance by their top soldiers. They’re typically worn on a special strip of fabric near the lapel, but soldiers from different countries sometimes wear them in other places. No matter how many _magical medals_ you have, they collectively count as one invested item.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Gorilla’s Might
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 25 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This steel medal resembles the head and upper body of a [gorilla](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2827). It’s typically given in recognition of physical prowess, and it grants you a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), and [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378).

**Activate—Gorila's Second Leap** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would fail but not critically fail an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378);  **Effect** The gorilla on the medal beats its chest, giving you another chance. You reroll the failed check.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Griffon’s Heart
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This copper medal features a [griffon’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3034) face, wings, and talons in profile. It is given in recognition of remarkable bravery, and it grants you a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects. While wearing this pendant, you can also cast [_forbidding ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1535) as an [innate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2901) cantrip.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of the Wolf Pack
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

There are three [wolf’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3241) heads engraved on this pewter medal, typically awarded to squads who demonstrate exceptional teamwork. While wearing the _medal of the wolf pack_, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against enemies you are [flanking](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 12"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Unicorn’s Purity
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 1,700 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The profile of the [unicorn](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=504) on this silver medal has a horn that extends slightly beyond the circular border. This medal is awarded in recognition of true righteousness and exemplary service to a cause.

**Activate—Unicorn’s Grace** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would regain Hit Points from a [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) effect;  **Effect** You regain an additional 4d6 Hit Points.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 16"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Phoenix’s Fire
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 9,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The [phoenix](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3137) on this gold medal is proud and fierce, and the medal features a border shaped like a flame. This medal is considered the highest honor in many countries and is awarded to those soldiers who have truly exemplified the ethics of their country through unbelievable service.

**Activate—Phoenix’s Sacrifice** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition increases;  **Effect** The phoenix bursts into flames. You lose the dying condition and regain 1 Hit Point. Your [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) value does not increase. You can use this action while [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95).

>
[Medic's Armband](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3972)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You wear this white armband with a bright blue symbol identifying you as a combat medic. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to change the attitudes of [diseased](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [poisoned](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), and [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) creatures.

**Activate—Do No Harm** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** An enemy within 30 feet targets you with a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or a spell that deals damage;  **Effect** Your armband glows, showing that you’re here as a medic and not as a combatant. Both you and the triggering enemy take a –4 status penalty to damage rolls until the end of your next turn.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medic’s Armband
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 10"
pfs="Standard"
>
Greater Medic’s Armband
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 152

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

You gain a +2 item bonus to [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) checks to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) and [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399), and the status penalty to damage rolls from Do No Harm increases to –8.

This [standard-grade dawnsilver shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2814) (Hardness 5, HP 20, BT 10) is inscribed with the symbol of a deity dedicated to [healing](/Domains.aspx?ID=78) and medicine. The shield is designed for combat medics to aid combatants or adventurers in the midst of battle. [Healer’s tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727) can be stored on the backside of this shield. This shield grants a +2 item bonus to [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) checks.

**Activate—Adrenaline Boost** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You grant a medicinal boost to bring someone back into the fray. You [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) to stabilize an adjacent ally with the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition. On a success, they gain 6d6+20 Hit Points, can immediately [Stand](/Actions.aspx?ID=2303) as a free action, and become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round. They can use this extra action only to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand **Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 145 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 3 **Base Weapon** [Longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386) --- **Perception** +11; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406) [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) 40 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) hearing 30 feet **Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) ([Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49), [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155)) **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +13, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +11, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +10, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +11 **Int** +2, **Wis** +3, **Cha** +5 **Will** +11 --- **_Nethys Note: This artifact contains spoilers for The Dead God's Hand. Read at your own risk._** Meloth's Lifedrinker is a _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_ whose blade appears to be made of obsidian pitted with pocks and scars that, upon closer examination, are tiny images of screaming faces, their haunted visages twisted in pain and fear. It was once a much more powerful weapon, until Sarnax used it as a prison to contain the essence of its original wielder—a demon lord named Meloth. The magic that once granted the blade its power immediately transformed and refocused into the task of serving as a prison for the demon lord, leaving the sword a shadow of its prior glory and infusing it with an unnatural weight three times that of a typical longsword. Over the centuries, Meloth has become able to observe and manipulate the world around the blade, as detailed in the adventure. Meloth's ability to influence the world around him via illusions is limited to those events detailed in the adventure, but a PC who ends up carrying the cursed sword for an extended length of time (beyond the scope of this adventure) might find similar illusions manifesting to further torment them, their companions, and anyone around them. Even then, Meloth won't directly communicate with his wielder unless he's fused to them. A character who holds Meloth's Lifedrinker must make a DC 18 Will save to resist Meloth's influence at the end of every round they continue to hold the weapon (one can safely—but awkwardly—transport _Meloth's Lifedrinker_ by picking it up, moving, and then dropping it before ending one's turn). **Critical Success** The character is temporarily immune to Meloth's influence for 24 hours and can carry or wield the sword normally as a _+1 longsword_.
**Success** The character is unaffected by Meloth’s influence this round.
**Failure** _Meloth's Lifedrinker_ [fuses with the character](/Rules.aspx?ID=3245). As part of this bond, Meloth absorbs some of the character's life, reducing the character's maximum HP by 6 (to a minimum of 1) for as long as the character remains fused to the sword. Meloth now communicates with the fused character via telepathy— encouraging them through lies, coercion, and threats to commit more and more atrocities while seeking a way to somehow free him from this prison.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but it reduces the character’s maximum HP by 12 (to a minimum of 1). Meloth's Lifedrinker (Improved) **Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 145 --- If during the first interlude of the Test of Aroden a PC allows Meloth to awaken the blade, the result empowers Meloth's Lifedrinker into a _+1 striking [wounding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2854) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_. As long as a character carries _Meloth's Lifedrinker_, they can speak and understand [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114). In addition, this empowered version of the blade gains the following activations. **Activate—Lifedrink** ([death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) **Trigger** _Meloth's Lifedrinker_ scores a critical hit on a living creature with a level equal to or higher than its wielder; **Effect** _Meloth's Lifedrinker_ inflicts 1d6 additional void damage to the living creature. If the creature struck by the critical hit is slain by its damage, the blade impales its victim. Black, oily energy like wet smoke pours from the victim's eyes and flows to the ebon sword, desiccating the corpse in an instant as all of its liquid seeps into the Lifedrinker, leaving the body a dried-out husk. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 10th level, _Meloth's Lifedrinker's_ _+1 weapon potency_ rune permanently becomes a _+2 weapon potency_ rune. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 12th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's _striking_ rune permanently becomes a _greater striking_ rune. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 16th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's _+2 weapon potency_ rune permanently becomes a _+3 weapon potency_ rune. And the first time this happens when its wielder is at least 19th level, _Meloth's Lifedrinker's_ _greater striking_ rune permanently becomes a _major striking_ rune. **Activate—Vision of Meloth** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** _Meloth's Lifedrinker_ causes a creature within 60 feet to experience a harrowing vision in which Meloth, as he appeared in life (a vaguely [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) horned [demon](/Traits.aspx?ID=573) not quite [bat](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=369) nor [leech](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=606) nor blood-drinking [fly](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=594)), leaps from the blade to surge forward and devour the target. The wielder of _Meloth's Lifedrinker_ sees this as well, but no other observers do. The targeted creature takes 6d6 mental damage with a Will save; the DC is equal to the wielder's class or spell DC, whichever is higher. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this effect, the vision becomes reality and kills the target instantly. Onlookers see only the target swiftly and gorily consumed by unseen mouths over the course of a few seconds, after which a mutilated carcass drops to the ground, lifeless. As an intelligent weapon, _Meloth's Lifedrinker_ can activate this ability on a whim, and often does so when the sword senses a creature that would be likely to die as a result of this activation—be that creature friend or foe of the wielder. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes half damage and is [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1.
**Failure** The target takes full damage and is frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** The target takes double damage, is frightened 4, and is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 as long as it remains frightened. Meloth's Lifedrinker **Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 145

The magic that once granted the blade its power immediately transformed and refocused into the task of serving as a prison for the demon lord, leaving the sword a shadow of its prior glory and infusing it with an unnatural weight three times that of a typical longsword. Over the centuries, Meloth has become able to observe and manipulate the world around the blade, as detailed in the adventure. Meloth's ability to influence the world around him via illusions is limited to those events detailed in the adventure, but a PC who ends up carrying the cursed sword for an extended length of time (beyond the scope of this adventure) might find similar illusions manifesting to further torment them, their companions, and anyone around them. Even then, Meloth won't directly communicate with his wielder unless he's fused to them. A character who holds Meloth's Lifedrinker must make a DC 18 Will save to resist Meloth's influence at the end of every round they continue to hold the weapon (one can safely—but awkwardly—transport Meloth's Lifedrinker by picking it up, moving, and then dropping it before ending one's turn). Critical Success The character is temporarily immune to Meloth's influence for 24 hours and can carry or wield the sword normally as a +1 longsword . Success The character is unaffected by Meloth’s influence this round. Failure Meloth's Lifedrinker fuses with the character. As part of this bond, Meloth absorbs some of the character's life, reducing the character's maximum HP by 6 (to a minimum of 1) for as long as the character remains fused to the sword. Meloth now communicates with the fused character via telepathy— encouraging them through lies, coercion, and threats to commit more and more atrocities while seeking a way to somehow free him from this prison. Critical Failure As failure, but it reduces the character’s maximum HP by 12 (to a minimum of 1). Item 7 Meloth's Lifedrinker (Improved) Source The Dead God's Hand pg. 145 If during the first interlude of the Test of Aroden a PC allows Meloth to awaken the blade, the result empowers Meloth's Lifedrinker into a +1 striking wounding longsword . As long as a character carries Meloth's Lifedrinker , they can speak and understand Chthonian. In addition, this empowered version of the blade gains the following activations. Activate—Lifedrink Reaction (death, divine, void) Trigger Meloth's Lifedrinker scores a critical hit on a living creature with a level equal to or higher than its wielder; Effect Meloth's Lifedrinker inflicts 1d6 additional void damage to the living creature. If the creature struck by the critical hit is slain by its damage, the blade impales its victim. Black, oily energy like wet smoke pours from the victim's eyes and flows to the ebon sword, desiccating the corpse in an instant as all of its liquid seeps into the Lifedrinker, leaving the body a dried-out husk. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 10th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's +1 weapon potency rune permanently becomes a +2 weapon potency rune. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 12th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's striking rune permanently becomes a greater striking rune. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 16th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's +2 weapon potency rune permanently becomes a +3 weapon potency rune. And the first time this happens when its wielder is at least 19th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's greater striking rune permanently becomes a major striking rune. Activate—Vision of Meloth Two Actions (concentrate, death, emotion, fear, mental) Frequency once per day; Effect Meloth's Lifedrinker causes a creature within 60 feet to experience a harrowing vision in which Meloth, as he appeared in life (a vaguely humanoid horned demon not quite bat nor leech nor blood-drinking fly), leaps from the blade to surge forward and devour the target. The wielder of Meloth's Lifedrinker sees this as well, but no other observers do. The targeted creature takes 6d6 mental damage with a Will save; the DC is equal to the wielder's class or spell DC, whichever is higher. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this effect, the vision becomes reality and kills the target instantly. Onlookers see only the target swiftly and gorily consumed by unseen mouths over the course of a few seconds, after which a mutilated carcass drops to the ground, lifeless. As an intelligent weapon, Meloth's Lifedrinker can activate this ability on a whim, and often does so when the sword senses a creature that would be likely to die as a result of this activation—be that creature friend or foe of the wielder. Critical Success The target is unaffected. Success The target takes half damage and is frightened 1. Failure The target takes full damage and is frightened 2. Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is frightened 4, and is slowed 1 as long as it remains frightened. Item 4 Meloth's Lifedrinker Source The Dead God's Hand pg. 145

As long as a character carries Meloth's Lifedrinker , they can speak and understand Chthonian. In addition, this empowered version of the blade gains the following activations. Activate—Lifedrink Reaction (death, divine, void) Trigger Meloth's Lifedrinker scores a critical hit on a living creature with a level equal to or higher than its wielder; Effect Meloth's Lifedrinker inflicts 1d6 additional void damage to the living creature. If the creature struck by the critical hit is slain by its damage, the blade impales its victim. Black, oily energy like wet smoke pours from the victim's eyes and flows to the ebon sword, desiccating the corpse in an instant as all of its liquid seeps into the Lifedrinker, leaving the body a dried-out husk. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 10th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's +1 weapon potency rune permanently becomes a +2 weapon potency rune. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 12th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's striking rune permanently becomes a greater striking rune. The first time this happens when its wielder is at least 16th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's +2 weapon potency rune permanently becomes a +3 weapon potency rune. And the first time this happens when its wielder is at least 19th level, Meloth's Lifedrinker's greater striking rune permanently becomes a major striking rune. Activate—Vision of Meloth Two Actions (concentrate, death, emotion, fear, mental) Frequency once per day; Effect Meloth's Lifedrinker causes a creature within 60 feet to experience a harrowing vision in which Meloth, as he appeared in life (a vaguely humanoid horned demon not quite bat nor leech nor blood-drinking fly), leaps from the blade to surge forward and devour the target. The wielder of Meloth's Lifedrinker sees this as well, but no other observers do. The targeted creature takes 6d6 mental damage with a Will save; the DC is equal to the wielder's class or spell DC, whichever is higher. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this effect, the vision becomes reality and kills the target instantly. Onlookers see only the target swiftly and gorily consumed by unseen mouths over the course of a few seconds, after which a mutilated carcass drops to the ground, lifeless. As an intelligent weapon, Meloth's Lifedrinker can activate this ability on a whim, and often does so when the sword senses a creature that would be likely to die as a result of this activation—be that creature friend or foe of the wielder. Critical Success The target is unaffected. Success The target takes half damage and is frightened 1. Failure The target takes full damage and is frightened 2. Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is frightened 4, and is slowed 1 as long as it remains frightened. Item 4 Meloth's Lifedrinker Source The Dead God's Hand pg. 145

---

These braided wool cords are threaded with reflective metal threads in patterns specified by the purchaser. No two society's patterns are the same, and purchasers tend to return to the same weaver each time to ensure new cords match previous ones. In a room lit only by dim candlelight, the reflective metal threads shimmer in a specific pattern. Many societies use these cords to prevent outsiders from infiltrating secret meetings and often have someone at the meeting area's entrance checking cords before allowing entry.

[Memoir Map](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2210)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 120

**Price** 13 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Your journeys and the major events in your life that occur after you obtain this tattoo appear on it, your life story traced upon your skin. Each time you journey somewhere new or accomplish something noteworthy to you, a design or symbol appears, representing the event. The positions of these images are relative in location, but measurements aren't exact. A _memoir map_ starts with an icon representing your location when you receive the tattoo, usually over the heart, and grows from there. Traveling to another plane causes a new portion to appear on a different part of your body to represent that plane. If you want a record of your life before you receive your _memoir map_, you can have the tattoo artist embellish the map to represent past events.

</title>

<traits>

**Bulk** L

---

This simple guitar appears worn and battered from use, but upon close observation, the damage seems to be intentional. From the correct angle, the guitar's scratches and marks seem to form a simple picture, such as an environmental scene or a crude face.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You play music with the guitar and the instrument's power shares a memory with your audience. When sharing with an audience, you share a memory of yours with anyone within 30 feet. This has the effects of [_mindlink_](/Spells.aspx?ID=195) for anyone that can hear the music.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per month;   **Effect** You play the guitar and the instrument attempts to help you recover a lost memory. You can either have a specific memory in mind, such as trying to remember a childhood event, or let the guitar find a memory for you. You recall the moment with perfect clarity and reestablish it permanently in your mind with the failure effects of [_modify memory_](/Spells.aspx?ID=200).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 14"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Memory Palace](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1374)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 80

**Price** 4,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk**  when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _memory palace_ is an elaborate magical structure that safely stores memories for easy access. It appears to be a miniature Taldan villa small enough to fit in the palm of a human hand.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> (10 minutes) envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The miniature grows into a building connected to the [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=8) for 1 hour. The _memory palace_ has a 30-foot-square central courtyard surrounded by 12 10-foot-square chambers. Arranged within these chambers are various items referred to as the palace's nodes—statues, tapestries, fountains, and other works of art are common, but a node can take other forms at the GM's discretion. As a 10-minute activity, you can imprint one extended memory onto a node: the contents of a specific simple book, for example, or the events of a recent adventure. When you do, the node changes its shape and appearance to visually represent the memory you have imprinted onto it. If the node was already imprinted with a memory, the old one can be overwritten to repurpose the node.

 Memories you have imprinted on a node can be mentally accessed at any time by a creature holding the memory palace in its miniature form, regardless of who imprinted them. This grants a +2 item bonus to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) checks relating to details specifically occurring within the memory. What exactly qualifies is up to the GM's discretion, but a node shouldn't grant the benefits for most uses of a given skill. For example, a node dedicated to a book about trees found in the Mwangi Expanse would help with Recall Knowledge checks for such trees, but it wouldn't grant the benefits for all [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks to Recall Knowledge.

 A _memory palace_ node can also store the text from a [spellbook](/Equipment.aspx?ID=53) or magical tome, but these memories aren't a substitute for having the book in your possession. A wizard can't prepare spells from a memory palace, though they could use it as source material to try to [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=25). However, since storing spells in a node would only benefit someone else who later discovers the _memory palace_, few choose to take such an action. The memories contained within the nodes aren't real, and thus don't cause harmful effects, even if the source of the memory was a mental danger. Many _memory palaces_ have leftover memories from previous users—now long dead—imprinted on their various nodes.

</column>

The time-honored tradition of weaving beautiful, embroidered glory ribbons throughout one’s hair and beard remains an important cultural practice among some dwarven clans, with the choice of colors and style of presentation representing status, achievements, and other significant aspects of someone’s position. Magical versions also exist that help enhance the wearer’s memory. These magical ribbons are especially popular when someone has been invited to serve as a toastmaster at a guild banquet or as a master of ceremonies at an important festival. Their use in final oral exams for high positions is, however, hotly debated.

**Activate—Read the Ribbon's Story** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You attempt a skill check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) but haven’t rolled yet;  **Effect** The _memory ribbon_ grants you a +2 item bonus to the triggering skill check to Recall Knowledge. Afterward, the ribbon becomes non-magical.

---

This hot, broth-based soup typically contains tubers, leeks, zesty spices, reagents, and if desired, the meat of livestock. Civic authorities commission batches of mender's soup for workers if a tricky job is on the agenda. After you eat the soup, its effects last 24 hours or until you make your next daily preparations, whichever comes first. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks to [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) and restore an additional 5 Hit Points to items you successfully Repair during this time. 

If you eat mender's soup over the entire period required to attempt a Crafting check to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) (typically a minimum of eating the soup each day for 4 days), the +1 bonus from the soup can be applied to that check, too.

After you eat the soup, its effects last 24 hours or until you make your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), whichever comes first. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) checks to [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) and restore an additional 5 Hit Points to items you successfully Repair during this time. 

If you eat mender’s soup over the entire period required to attempt a Crafting check to Craft (typically a minimum of eating the soup each day for 4 days), the +1 bonus from the soup can be applied to that check, too.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 33

**Price** 70 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

_Merciful_ weapons are sheathed in an unmistakable wispy green aura recognized by both gladiators and guards around the world. A merciful weapon has the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) trait and can't be used to make a lethal attack. Any [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) the weapon would deal is negated.

 On a critical hit, a _merciful_ weapon causes the target to become [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) with the weapon's wielder for 1 minute, as the target is bombarded with feelings of guilt and remorse. This is a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect. If you have access to the weapon's [critical specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=235), you choose whether to use it or the merciful effect.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 187 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn cloak **Bulk** L --- This deep red cloak fits lightly about your shoulders, and the edges perpetually twitch slightly, as though caught in a breeze. The cloth feels smoother than silk, rippling and swaying like liquid when in motion. You feel a lively energy infusing your arms and legs. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) and [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15), and a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against attacks from reactions triggered by your movement. When you invest the cloak, you either increase your Dexterity score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An enemy misses you with a melee Strike; **Effect** You slip around the attacking creature with ease. You Step, without moving away from the triggering enemy, and then make a melee Strike against the triggering enemy if it's within reach. If you do make a Strike, the target attempts a DC 38 Perception check before you roll. **Failure** This creature is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against the Strike.
**Critical Failure** This creature is flat-footed against all your attacks until the end of their next turn. **Activate** command, envision ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The cloak hums with power as your whirl it around yourself, disappearing amid a brief flash of light. Teleport up to double your Speed to a location you can see. At the end of the teleportation, you can make a melee Strike against a creature within reach, if there is one.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Messenger Missive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4597)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Missive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=485" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 85

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>envision, Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _messenger missive_ sends itself. When composing the missive, you write a location upon it. You can also include an individual creature you expect to be in that location as a recipient; if you don’t, the first creature in the location to touch the missive is treated as the recipient. Once you finish composing the missive, it folds itself into the shape of a bird and Flies at a Speed of 45 feet (15 miles per hour) toward the location for up to 24 hours. It alights near its recipient or in their hand. When activated, the missive becomes non-magical but retains its contents. If it fails to reach its recipient in 24 hours, the missive burns to ash.

This sphere contains small fragments of [thunderstones](/Equipment.aspx?ID=79) within a colloidal suspension of a precious metal. When you twist the sphere, it creates an opaque mist in a burst centered on one corner of your space. Creatures within that area are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and all other creatures are concealed to them. Any creature with a weakness to the precious metal that starts its turn in the mist takes damage equal to its weakness. The mist lasts for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind. Most metalmist spheres are filled with [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=277) or [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=272), but more expensive versions containing other ingredients might exist.

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This craggy stone ammunition is warm to the touch. When you fire an activated _meteor shot,_ it explodes into a small swarm of meteors as it reaches its target, scorching nearby creatures and littering the ground with rubble. In addition to the weapon's normal damage, the meteor shot deals fire damage and the ground in the area becomes difficult terrain.

 In addition, the Strike gains the following critical failure effect.

**Critical Failure** The weapon misfires.

[Metronomic Hammer](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1595)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #179: Cradle of Quartz](/Sources.aspx?ID=122) pg. 79

**Price** 160 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 or 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Gnome Hooked Hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=52)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A polished brass metronome ticks rhythmically within the haft of this _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [gnome hooked hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=52)_. Gnome adherents of [Brigh](/Deities.aspx?ID=33) often attempt to reproduce this item as part of a ritual symbolizing methodical problem-solving and thoughtful craftsmanship.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;   **Trigger** You attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) a creature with the _metronomic hammer_;  **Effect** By timing the sweeping arcs of your Trip attempt to the built-in metronome of a _metronomic hammer_, you gain a +1 item bonus to your [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to Trip the target. This item bonus increases by 1 with every subsequent Trip attempt you make with the _metronomic hammer_ against the same target this turn, to a maximum of +3 on your third Trip. The bonus resets to +1 if you successfully Trip the target, if you critically fail to Trip the target, or if your turn ends.

    pfs="Limited"
>
[Metuak's Pendant](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1525)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley](/Sources.aspx?ID=113) pg. 81

**Price** 155 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black quartz pendant carved in the shape of an [angel's](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=3) feather hangs from a leather cord worn around the neck. Once worn by Metuak of the Burning Mammoths, this family heirloom anchors you to your ancestors, preserving your sense of self and protecting your mind from mental manipulation and demonic possession. You gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects that would make you [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6), [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37). This bonus increases to +2 if the source of the effect is a [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=70).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" />  ;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You succeed or critically succeed at a saving throw against a mental effect that would make you confused, controlled, frightened, or stupefied;  **Effect** Empowered by your determination, your ancestors protect you and your nearby allies. For 1 minute, you and each of your allies within 30 feet gains a +1 status bonus to saving throws against mental effects that would make you confused, controlled, frightened, or stupefied.
